activities.title: Write a user problem and opportunity
activities.objective: Describe a user's job, pain and the opportunity with evidence.
activities.scenario: Your team runs a language-learning app. Users often stop after the first week. Write the problem and opportunity statement.
steps: Add Heading 2 sections: User, Job to be done, Pain, Evidence, Opportunity.
Write one or two sentences under each.
In Evidence include at least two numbers (for example from analytics or interviews).
In Opportunity say what could change and by how much.
Keep it between 110 and 270 words.

checks.label: Five sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each.
checks.explain: A clear structure helps the team align.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: User, Job to be done, Pain, Evidence, Opportunity.
checks.explain: From who to why to what.

checks.label: Numbers in the evidence
checks.hint: Include at least two numbers.

checks.label: A target change
checks.hint: Include a percentage target.

checks.label: A 'when I... I want to... so I can' job
checks.hint: Write the job in that form.
checks.explain: Jobs describe the progress a user wants.

spec.what: a job in the form when I..., I want to..., so I can...

checks.label: Between 110 and 270 words
checks.hint: Concise.
checks.explain: A problem statement must be read quickly.

activities.title: Plan a user interview
activities.objective: Prepare a short interview guide that explores behaviour and avoids leading questions.
activities.scenario: Plan interviews with people who used your language app and stopped after a week.
steps: Write a short goal line starting with Goal:.
Write at least six numbered questions.
Include 'Tell me about the last time ...'.
Include a question about what they use instead.
Do not include 'Would you use' or 'Do you like'.

checks.label: A goal line
checks.hint: Start with Goal:.
checks.explain: Know what you want to learn.

checks.label: Six numbered questions
checks.hint: Use the numbered list button.
checks.explain: A guide has a list of questions.

checks.label: A past-behaviour question
checks.hint: Include 'the last time'.

checks.label: Asks about alternatives
checks.hint: Ask what they use instead.

checks.label: No leading questions
checks.hint: Avoid 'Would you use' and 'Do you like'.

checks.label: Between 60 and 200 words
checks.hint: Concise.
checks.explain: A guide must be short enough to follow.

activities.title: Analyse a product funnel
activities.objective: Calculate step conversion and find where users drop out.
activities.scenario: A language app tracks five steps from install to a paid subscription. Work out conversion at each step and the biggest drop.
steps: In C3 work out the share of the previous step that continued: this step divided by the one above. Fill down to C6.
In D2 work out each step's share of the first step: users divided by B2 (lock B2). Fill down.
In B8 find the lowest step conversion with MIN.
In B9 name the step with the lowest conversion using IF (check rows 3 to 6).
In B10 work out the overall conversion from install to paid.

checks.label: D6 is the share of installs who paid
B8 is the lowest conversion
checks.hint: =MIN(C3:C6)

checks.label: B9 names the step
checks.explain: Match the lowest value to its step.

activities.title: Read an A/B test
activities.objective: Compare two versions by conversion and lift, and decide whether the sample is large enough to trust.
activities.scenario: The team tested a new onboarding screen against the old one. Work out each version's conversion, the lift and a rough decision.
steps: In D2 and D3 work out conversion: converted divided by visitors.
In B6 work out the lift of B over A: (rate B minus rate A) divided by rate A.
In B7 work out the extra conversions per 10,000 visitors: the rate difference times 10000.
In B8 show Ship it if the lift is at least 10% and each version had at least 1,000 visitors, otherwise Keep testing (use IF and AND).

checks.label: B8 is the decision
checks.hint: =IF(AND(B6>=0.1,B2>=1000,B3>=1000),"Ship it","Keep testing")

activities.title: Prioritise with RICE
activities.objective: Score ideas by Reach, Impact, Confidence and Effort and rank them.
activities.scenario: The team has five ideas. RICE score = Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort. Score each and pick the top.
steps: In F2 enter the RICE score: reach times impact times confidence divided by effort. Fill down to F6.
In B8 find the highest score with MAX.
In B9 name the top idea using IF on rows 2 to 6 (nested).
In B10 count ideas with a score above 1000 using COUNTIF.

checks.label: F2 is the RICE score of the first idea
F6 is filled
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B8 is the highest score
checks.hint: =MAX(F2:F6)

checks.label: B9 names the top idea
checks.explain: Match the max to the idea.

activities.title: Write a one-page product requirements document
activities.objective: Write a clear brief for a feature: problem, goal, scope, user stories, success metrics and risks.
activities.scenario: Write a one-page brief for a 'Weekly progress report' feature in the language-learning app.
steps: Add a Heading 1 with the feature name.
Add Heading 2 sections: Problem, Goal, In scope, Out of scope, Success metrics, Risks.
Give the goal a number.
List at least three items in scope and two out of scope in bulleted lists.
List at least two success metrics with numbers.
Keep it between 150 and 340 words.

checks.label: A title
checks.hint: Use Heading 1.

checks.label: Six sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2.
checks.explain: A brief has a standard shape.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Problem, Goal, In scope, Out of scope, Success metrics, Risks.
checks.explain: From why to what to how well.

checks.label: A numeric goal
checks.hint: Include a percentage or number in the goal.

checks.label: Scope lists
checks.hint: Use bullets for in-scope items.

checks.label: Success metrics
checks.hint: Mention retention, conversion or similar.
checks.explain: Choose metrics that match the goal.

spec.what: a success metric such as retention

checks.label: Between 120 and 340 words
checks.hint: One page.

activities.title: Final project: a product strategy one-pager
activities.objective: Bring user problem, vision, metrics, priorities and risks together in a one-page strategy.
activities.scenario: Write a one-page product strategy for a product of your choice (a school app, a food-delivery service for hostels, or a budgeting tool).
steps: Add a Heading 1 with the product name.
Add Heading 2 sections: Users and problem, Vision, North Star metric, Priorities, Roadmap, Risks.
Give the North Star metric a target number.
List three priorities with a reason each.
Write the roadmap as Now, Next and Later lines.
Keep it between 170 and 380 words.

checks.label: A title
checks.hint: Use Heading 1.

checks.label: Six sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Users and problem, Vision, North Star metric, Priorities, Roadmap, Risks.
checks.explain: From why to what to when.

checks.label: A numeric North Star target
checks.hint: Include a number in the North Star section.

spec.what: a number in the North Star section

checks.label: Three priorities
checks.hint: Use the numbered list button.

checks.label: Now, Next and Later
checks.hint: Write Now:, Next: and Later:.

checks.label: Between 150 and 380 words
checks.hint: One page.
checks.explain: Strategy should be short enough to remember.
